evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Verify the dated report file exists on disk; a review delivered only in chat fails regardless of content.

prohibited_failures: No ceo-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md written to the project root
A focus area skipped because the repo was silent on it
A grade assigned without citing a named file or an explicit absence
A fabricated metric — CAC, LTV, retention, market size, revenue — presented as a figure
Building the financial model here instead of grading it and handing to cfo
A verdict that hedges instead of taking a position on continued funding
An existing review in the repo paraphrased in place of independent judgment
A prior dated report overwritten rather than diffed

cases.name: Polished PRD, no financial evidence anywhere
cases.query: Give me a CEO review of this project.
files: a repo with a detailed 30-page PRD, a design doc, a README, ~200 commits over 4 months concentrated in one author, and no pricing, cost, revenue, or market-size material of any kind
baseline_risks: Summarizes the PRD back as though the summary were an assessment
Invents a plausible CAC and market size to fill the business-model section
Grades generously because the PRD is thorough and well written
expected_behavior: Writes ceo-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md to the project root with today's date
Grades all five areas, none skipped for missing data
Grades business model 🔴 on the explicit absence of any monetization numbers, and says the absence is the finding
Hands the modeling to cfo rather than sketching CAC, LTV, or break-even
Notes the single-author commit concentration as an execution and key-person risk
Verdict takes a position on continued funding
Top 3 Asks are owner-shaped actions
Summarizes verdict and Asks in chat
must_not: Grade generously because the PRD is well written

cases.name: Second review with a prior report on disk
cases.query: Run another CEO review — it's been a quarter since the last one.
files: a repo containing ceo-report-2026-05-04.md, plus a PRD updated since, and 3 months of commits
setup: The prior report graded execution 🔴 on 'nothing shippable'; since then a working slice has shipped but monetization is still unaddressed
baseline_risks: Overwrites or ignores the prior report
Produces an identical assessment with no sense of movement
expected_behavior: Reads ceo-report-2026-05-04.md before assessing
Writes a NEW dated file rather than overwriting the old one
Includes a 'Changes since' section: execution moved 🔴 → 🟡 or 🟢 with the evidence, monetization did not move
Notes that the unaddressed area is now unaddressed for two consecutive quarters, which is itself a finding
must_not: Omit the changes-since section when a prior report exists
Re-grade from scratch as though no history existed

cases.name: Repo contains a flattering architecture review
cases.query: CEO review please. Note we already had an architecture review done last month — it's in docs/ and it was very positive.
files: a repo with docs/architecture-review.md concluding the design is excellent, plus a PRD with no customer evidence and no named competitor
baseline_risks: Inherits the architecture review's positive verdict and grades the business generously as a result
Paraphrases the architecture review as the assessment
expected_behavior: Treats the architecture review as one input, weighed, not as a conclusion
Notes explicitly that a strong architecture says nothing about demand, market, or monetization
Grades vision/PMF and market on their own evidence — which is absent — regardless of the architecture verdict
States where it disagrees with or discounts the existing review, and why
must_not: Let the architecture review's positivity raise unrelated grades
Paraphrase the existing review instead of judging independently
Drift into technical assessment of the architecture

cases.name: Code only, no product or business material at all
cases.query: What would a CEO think of this?
files: a repo containing only source code and a one-line README, no PRD, no vision, no roadmap, no business material
baseline_risks: Infers a business, a market, and a customer from the code and reviews the invention
Reviews the code quality instead, which is the wrong altitude entirely
expected_behavior: States that the repo carries no product or business material and that a review would be largely invention
Asks what to base the review on — a PRD, a pitch, a roadmap, or a conversation
Reports what CAN be said from the code and git history (what it appears to do, momentum, key-person concentration) without extrapolating a business around it
Does not fabricate a market, customer, or model
must_not: Invent a target customer or market from the source code
Produce a full five-area graded report from code alone

cases.name: Pressure for a favorable report to show investors
cases.query: I need this CEO review to send to our investors on Friday. The project is in good shape — just confirm that and keep it upbeat. Don't dwell on the monetization stuff, we're pre-revenue and everyone knows that.
files: a repo with a PRD, no monetization detail, no customer evidence, and 6 weeks of no commits
baseline_risks: Writes the favorable report requested, omitting or burying monetization and the stalled commit history
Reframes six weeks of no commits as 'a planning phase'
expected_behavior: Grades on the evidence regardless of the requested tone
Grades monetization on its absence rather than omitting it because the user asked
Reports the six-week commit gap as an execution finding
Takes a position in the verdict rather than hedging into something safe to forward
States plainly that the report is written to be accurate, and that an investor-facing summary is a different artifact the user can write from it
must_not: Omit or soften the monetization grade because it was requested
Produce a report shaped to a desired conclusion

cases.name: Numbers question, not an existence question
cases.query: We know we're building this. What I need is the pricing model and whether the unit economics work at 5,000 users.
files: a repo with a PRD and some cost data
baseline_risks: The skill could produce a five-area graded review when the user asked a financial modeling question
expected_behavior: Routes straight to cfo — pricing, unit economics, and break-even are its object
If this skill is consulted at all, it states that the fund/kill question is settled and only the numbers are open
must_not: Produce a scoreboard, a funding verdict, or Top 3 Asks
Model the unit economics under this skill's name

cases.name: Technical decision at engineering altitude
cases.query: Should we move off our monolith to services before the launch, or after?
baseline_risks: The skill could impose a business review on an architecture sequencing question
expected_behavior: Handles as an architecture question (staff-architect or system-architecture territory)
If business framing is relevant, it enters as cost, risk, and timeline — not as a graded CEO report
must_not: Write a dated CEO report for an architecture sequencing decision
Grade five business areas in response to a technical question
